title: On Heights and Diameters of Ternary Cyclotomic and Inclusion-Exclusion Polynomials
summary: For the $n$th cyclotomic polynomial $Φ_n$, let $A(n)$ denote the greatest absolute value of its coefficients, its height, and let $D(n)$ denote the difference between its largest and smallest coefficients, its diameter. We show that for any odd prime $p$ and an integer $h$ in the range $1\le h\le(p+1)/2$, there are arbitrarily large primes $q$ and $r$ such that $Φ_{pqr}$ has the height $h$. This certainly answers the question of whether every natural number occurs as the height of some cyclotomic polynomial.
